title: SpringWater Retail — POS integration field notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick working notes from intake + technical scoping call with SpringWater retail (11/03 intake, follow-ups 12/12 and 02/27). This is a private-onramp candidate: they want low-latency POS augmentation (receipt parsing, upsell suggestion, fraud flagging) integrated into edge tills and a central reconciliation service.

Attendees (roles):
- Mark Delaney (SpringWater, Head of Retail Ops)
- Sophie Chen (SpringWater, Lead Platform Engineer)
- Priya Natarajan (Redwood Solutions)
- Marco Liu (Redwood SE)
- Aisha Grant (customer success)

High-level ask / pain:
- Improve cashier experience: extract structured items + totals from noisy OCR receipts and annotate likely loyalty matches in <300ms response at the POS.
- Provide in-line upsell text snippets for cashier or receipt print/send (multilingual: EN/ES/FR).
- On-device inference not required; hybrid: edge-forwarding to a nearby private-region Dedicated pool preferred.
- Must be PCI DSS compatible (no storage of PANs), and logs must scrub any card tokens or 2FA data.

Observed constraints & environment:
- POS tills are on managed Linux boxes; intermittent WAN (4G fallback), average RTT to their primary DC ~60-120ms.
- Average receipt size after OCR is ~800–1,200 characters (varies wildly).
- Peak concurrency: ~300 concurrent tills per region during lunchtime; expected QPS for inference ~150–200 requests/s at peak (batched traffic okay within 50–150ms extra latency budget).
- Single region deployment initially (US-East), plan to expand to EU via partner cloud.

Security & compliance notes:
- PCI: they asserted they only transmit tokenized PAN / last4 to Redwood if at all; however Sophie asked for explicit guidance on what to redact client-side.
- Want KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and audit logs shipped to their Splunk instance.
- Require data-retention policy: ephemeral request logs retained 7 days, aggregated metrics longer.

Model / inference preferences:
- Prefer small/medium open LLM family (instruction-tuned) for extraction and short-form upsell generation. Candidate models: 7B–13B quantized variants.
- Also evaluating specialized structured-extraction pipeline: smaller extractor model + downstream reranker.
- Strong preference for Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU) with fallback to Hosted API only for non-production.

Performance SLOs and cost targets:
- P95 end-to-end at POS (from request dispatch to response) <= 300ms for single-request path.
- Accept batching up to 3–5 concurrent receipts to reduce token cost for high-concurrency windows, but must keep tail latency constraints.
- Target cost target: <$0.002 per inference on average (ballpark asked by Finance).

Integration gotchas & risk items (from discussion / past experience):
1) OCR noise + line breaks: manifest as multi-line item descriptions and weird characters — extraction model must be robust to spurious characters and store/score confidence per field.
2) Receipt language mixing (EN + Spanish short phrases) — need bilingual tokenizer/embedding fallback or prefix language tag.
3) Intermittent network: local queuing at POS and graceful retry/backoff required; we should suggest a tiny local cache of recent common responses for fallback upsells.
4) PCI risk: accidentally returning full PANs in debugging traces — ensure redaction pipeline and strict logging policy.
5) Versioning: they want canary rollouts at store-cluster level (100 stores small canary -> 1000 -> global) and ability to revert quickly.
6) Edge TLS termination: they may want TLS at LB + mutual TLS to Redwood private endpoints.

Suggested Redwood config + patterns to propose:
- Dedicated pool per region with reserved capacity sized for p95 CPU/GPU headroom.
- Autoscale policy with burst capacity for lunch spikes and custom routing to nearby region if local pool saturated.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated receipts (loyalty lookups) and continuous batching window tuned to 20–40ms for low-latency small batches.
- Canary policy = store-cluster tags + traffic split 1%/5%/20% with automatic rollback on error rate/regression thresholds.
- KMS/HSM key import + audit-log forwarder to their Splunk (S3 sink with lifecycle 7d then analytics bucket).

Open technical questions for them (need answers before sizing pilot):
- Can they confirm that no raw PAN is ever forwarded from POS? (Sophie: yes tokenized, but need spec on token format and where truncation occurs)
- Do they have example OCR output (10–20 representative receipts) including worst-case noise and non-Latin scripts?
- What is average tokens generated for upsell text? (they guessed 12–20 tokens).
- Are there existing SLOs for reconciliation that would require synchronous ingestion of inferred structured data?
- Which stores will be in initial canary and can we get traffic patterns for those windows (historic QPS per store)?

Immediate next steps / action items (ownership + rough ETA):
- (Priya) Draft a one-pager pilot plan incl. sizing, cost estimate for Dedicated pool + burst (ETA 2026-03-10).
- (Marco) Build prototype adapter (POS->Redwood request/response minimal shim) and demo with 5 sample receipts; stubbed redaction (ETA 2026-03-20).
- (SpringWater / Sophie) Provide 20 anonymized OCR samples, and store list for canary (ETA 2026-03-08).
- (Aisha) Setup joint Slack channel and weekly check-ins; schedule operational runbook review (ETA 2026-03-05).
- (Priya) Send security checklist and proposed log-scrubbing rules for review by SpringWater security (ETA 2026-03-06).

Low-effort prototype plan (what to show in week 1):
- Live demo: take 5 real receipts -> OCR (customer) -> send to prototype adapter -> extractor model returns structured JSON + 1-line upsell suggestion.
- Show latency histogram (client-measured) and simple cost estimate.

Notes to self / talking points for next call:
- Emphasize that Dedicated lets them control tail latencies + avoids noisy neighbors; highlight canary and rollback controls in Redwood Console.
- Walk through redaction examples live — show how we detect and mask PAN-like patterns.
- Prepare quick ROI calc: uplift from 0.4% to 1.2% average transaction upsell conversion -> translate to monthly revenue for their avg ticket.

Rough risks that might block next step:
- If they transmit unredacted PANs we will need legal + PCI scoping and likely an on-prem enclave option (longer timeline).
- If OCR variability is extreme we may need multi-step pipeline (cleaner + extractor) which will increase latency and cost.

Reference snippets from call (verbatim-ish):
- Mark D: "We need something that just works at the checkout — if it slows down the line, we can't deploy."
- Sophie: "We will need mutual TLS; our infra team won't accept shared secrets without KMS-backed rotation."

File history / context:
- This is a user-level scratchpad capturing intake details; final proposal will live in Confluence and an internal pilot PR will be opened in github repo listed above.

-- end of scratchbook --
